title: The query complexity of uniformity testing with purified unitary access

comparators.scope: Twelve fixed targets: promise-only adaptive, globally bounded adaptive and fixed-unitary lower bounds; actual Lemmas1/2; full adversary/query norms, progress, preparation and prior probability.
Real added premise against all12 fixed source contracts.
Real unauthorized axiom against all12 fixed source contracts.

main_results.scope: A positive universal c gives Q ≥ c·min(d^(1/3)/ε^(4/3), √d/ε) for d ≥ 2, 0 < ε < 1/2 and promise-only adaptive testers with success ≥ .99, relative to the four explicit standard inputs.
The adaptive theorem includes measurements, branch-dependent directions and early stopping via AdaptiveNormalizationLaw; the fixed-unitary variant uses the other three standard inputs.
The actual Fourier–Dirichlet adversary and complete reflection queries, including whole radial complements, satisfy the printed norm bound with constant 20, relative to DirichletJointMomentLaw.
The actual continuous Dirichlet event has probability at least 1/144 for d ≥ 2 and a ≥ 1, relative to DirichletJointMomentLaw.
The fixed-unitary lower bound uses the exact 4Q collision-query reduction and explicit Dirichlet joint-moment, ninefold amplification and Kutin collision inputs.
